title: The end of the crisis of imagination
summary: From lost futures to new collective politics.
body:
Course themes

  • Capitalist realism and lost futures
  • A critique of the crisis of imagination
  • The material conditions of political action
  • Desire and collective organisation
  • Housing, the commons and community infrastructure

What will we work on?

Identifying how new political horizons are built materially and what role culture and critical thought can play in that.

Context and approach

From Mark Fisher to the debates on the cancellation of the future, the crisis of political imagination has been a recurring explanation for the limits of the left. The course connects it with precarity, the housing crisis, the decline of public services and the loss of spaces for social life.

Housing struggles, trade unionism, new socialisms and community infrastructure will help us analyse how collective capacities are built. The question of the future thus becomes a question about the institutions, resources and organisation that can sustain it.
introduction: Do we lack images of a different future, or the conditions to make it possible? We will revisit the debates on capitalist realism in the light of today’s struggles and forms of organisation.
